dedupe_keys.name: german energy efficiency register for data centres rzreg

description: The Energy Efficiency Register for Data Centres (Energieeffizienzregister für Rechenzentren, RZReg) is Germany's national register of data centres set up under the Energy Efficiency Act (Energieeffizienzgesetz) of 2023. Operators of data centres with a non-redundant rated power of 300 kW or more must report information about each facility every year, by 31 March for the previous calendar year, and larger ones also have duties on energy management, efficiency targets and use of waste heat. Reported data cover energy consumption and its renewable share, power usage effectiveness, reuse of waste heat, facility size and technical characteristics. Facilities of 500 kW and above first reported by 15 August 2024 and those of 300 to 500 kW by 1 July 2025. The public part of the register (Öffentliches RZReg) shows annual reports of individual data centres where the operator publishes them there, and aggregated statistics on an interactive map of Germany; the ministry also publishes a guide to all data points in German and English. Coverage: data centres of 300 kW and above in Germany, reporting year 2023 onward. Format and access: public web platform with reports and aggregates, free; facility-level data only where operators publish. Caveats: early years had delayed and incomplete reporting; aggregate categories hide individual sites. Simulation uses: national data-centre energy demand and efficiency baselines, waste heat potential for district heating models, and siting studies. Related records: the EU data centre energy performance database is the European counterpart that German reports feed.
